## Takeaways

So what does all of this even mean? It all boils down to this: not all state representations are created equal. 
If this CW framework performs so poorly in a test like this then why is it used so frequently? As we've seen, for close-proximity 
missions over short time horizons, CW still does a solid job at representing uncertainty --- and Cartesian RIC offsets are much 
more intuitive to visualize than orbital elements. When separations grow or you are propagating the uncertainty over longer horizons (or include J2 perturbations), 
switching to ROEs keeps linear covariance propagation accurate. Every framework has trade-offs, and it's up to mission designers to understand 
their environment and choose the framework that fits best.
